messages:
alex_eng: Hey team — legal gender marker and name change for my 17yo dependent finalized 2026-06-15. Need to update coverage records before open enrollment. What docs do you need and will carrier accept the change without new SSN?

rebecca_benefits: Congrats on getting that done, @alex_eng. Carriers accept legal name/gender changes with government-issued documentation. We need a copy of the court order or amended birth certificate and photo ID if available. SSN shouldn't change; no new SSN required.

maria_hrlegal: Confirming: as long as the legal change is documented (court order or state amendment), we can update internal records. If the dependent is 17, still eligible as a dependent until aging out rules. For any privacy/sensitivity concerns, we can flag the file as restricted access.

oliver_payroll: Payroll/benefits tax note: name/gender changes don't affect withholding or premiums. If you want payroll name updated on dependent lines we need the same docs so our systems match carrier files. No retro premium or tax changes expected.

benefits-bot: Please upload documents here: https://benefits.redwood.com/qle -> choose "Dependent name/gender change" and attach the court order or amended birth cert. Use effective date 2026-06-15. We will forward to carrier.

alex_eng: Appreciate it. One question: will the dependent get a new insurance ID card or will carrier keep same ID? Also worried about school records showing old name and coverage verification requests.

rebecca_benefits: Typically carriers issue new ID cards reflecting updated name/gender, but some carriers keep the same ID number and just update the demographic fields. We will request cards and provide a verification letter you can give to the school. If school needs a letter earlier, we can generate an employer verification with the case number.

maria_hrlegal: If you prefer, we can redact sensitive fields on the verification letter and certify coverage without broadcasting previous names. DM me and we'll craft a privacy-sensitive letter.

alex_eng: That would be great  please redact prior name. I'll upload the court order now. Also: does this affect open enrollment dependent verification? I worry they will reject if docs look different during OE.

rebecca_benefits: For open enrollment, carriers will cross-reference our submission. If docs are already in the case file we should be fine. We'll mark the case and notify OE team. Case created: NG-2026-2017.

oliver_payroll: Once docs are uploaded and benefits approves, we sync HRIS and payroll within 2 business days. No action needed on your end for OE beyond confirming dependent is still listed.

alex_eng: Uploaded court order and requested the redacted letter from @maria_hrlegal. Thanks everyone. Feels good to have this handled before OE. :relieved:
